body: "DO NOT AUDIT LEAN DECLARATION EXISTENCE WITH A REGEX -- use the graph; three\
  \ false conclusions in one session came from this\n\nThe pattern, which cost me\
  \ and two subagents real time in run 0054 s0010 and will recur: you\nwant to know\
  \ whether a \\lean{Name} pin resolves, or whether a declaration exists, so you grep\n\
  for '^(theorem|lemma|def|instance) Name'. That regex is wrong in at least three\
  \ ways, all of\nwhich occur in AJC:\n\n  1. ATTRIBUTE PREFIX. The declaration is\
  \ written  @[simp] lemma sectionsCast_refl ...  so the\n     keyword is not at line\
  \ start. This produced SIX false \"pin does not resolve\" findings on\n     Picard_SectionGradedRing.tex\
  \ nodes whose pins are in fact fine.\n  2. UNIVERSE-BINDER SUFFIX ON THE NAME. Written\
  \  theorem toSheaf_preservesFiniteColimits.{v', u', w'} ...\n     so the identifier\
  \ is followed by \".{\" rather than whitespace. Exactly four declarations in\n \
  \    AJC use this. Horizon's own graph scanner has the SAME bug (filed as I-0452),\
  \ so here the\n     regex and the tool are wrong together -- the worst case, because\
  \ agreement looks like\n     confirmation.\n  3. NAMESPACE CONTEXT. A bare name\
  \ says nothing about the fully-qualified name; you must find\n     the enclosing\
  \ namespace/end block, and an \"open\" can make the source text differ from the\n\
  \     pin.\n\nWHAT TO DO INSTEAD, in increasing order of authority:\n  - horizon\
  \ graph -p PROJECT get decl:Fully.Qualified.Name    -- resolves, or says \"no node\n\
  \    matching\". Same index the DAG is built from.\n  - horizon graph -p PROJECT\
  \ sync --blueprint TEX --lean DIR  -- read its warnings; this is the\n    definitive\
  \ list of unresolved pins and it cross-checks every pin at once.\n  - horizon search\
  \ NAME  -- spans all projects AND mathlib, which a grep cannot.\n  - A scratch file\
  \ with  #print axioms Fully.Qualified.Name  under lake env lean -- the only\n  \
  \  check that is not a text search at all, and the one that settles both existence\
  \ and whether\n    the thing is proved.\n\nTHE GENERALISABLE POINT, beyond Lean:\
  \ when auditing a CLAIM about the codebase, prefer the tool\nthat owns the index\
  \ over a pattern you wrote in the moment -- and when the two disagree, find\nout\
  \ WHY before believing either. In this session the graph was right about the six\
  \ and wrong\nabout the two, and in both cases the reason was visible in the declaration's\
  \ own source line.\n\nSHELL FOOTNOTE, since it corrupted the first version of this\
  \ very note: do not pass long prose\ncontaining backticks or $(...) to horizon inbox\
  \ add via an inline shell argument. Backticks are\ncommand substitution and will\
  \ silently splice command output into the body. Write the body to a\nfile and pass\

##### I-0456.yaml
id: I-0456
provider: local
kind: memory
body: "NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS\
  \ CONCLUSION\n\nDurable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump\
  \ (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).\n\nThe pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`,\
  \ presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit)\
  \ whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect:\
  \ hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines\n  rw\
  \ [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring\nbecause degK is\
  \ an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where\
  \ `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check,\
  \ no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is\
  \ true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at\
  \ one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional\
  \ proof of something whose other direction is free.\n\nThe check to run before claiming\
  \ a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three\
  \ lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every\
  \ `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.\n\nSecond lesson, on how to answer a vacuity\
  \ question properly. \"Is H consistent\" is nearly always answerable degenerately\
  \ (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative\
  \ questions are:\n  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);\n  - WHERE\
  \ is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold\
  \ and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof\
  \ that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every\
  \ bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single\
  \ prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than\
  \ \"consistent, vacuously\".\nA conditional refutation (one taking the thing it\
  \ refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much\
  \ weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.\n\nThird,\
  \ a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric`\
  \ as \"producing a real prime divisor on a curve\". The name does not resolve (no\
  \ such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and\
  \ the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one —\
  \ the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean)\
  \ and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed,\
  \ not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity\
  \ witness."

body: 'DECISION NEEDED: the rational-point hypothesis, and the blueprint describing
  an abandoned route.


  Two things surfaced by an adversarially-verified six-front assessment on 2026-07-27
  that only you can settle. Both outrank every mechanical improvement in flight.


  1. THE RATIONAL POINT. references/challenge.lean declares ''Jacobian C'' with NO
  rational-point binder. But instHasPicScheme (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316)
  makes ''[HasRationalPoint C]'' an ESSENTIAL hypothesis, and correctly so -- without
  a section, Pic(C x_k T) / pi_T^* Pic(T) need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman''s
  theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed
  to be a platform limitation; it is not. Mathlib v4.31 does carry the etale topology
  (.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50). So it
  is a design choice, and as the tree stands the project would prove something strictly
  weaker than the challenge asks. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept
  the weaker theorem and say so. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until
  it is settled. Roadmap node AJC.picrep.rational-point.


  2. THE BLUEPRINT ADVERTISES A ROUTE THE TREE ABANDONED. informal/pic-representability-campaign.md
  (2026-07-09) selected route D3 Milne-Kollar -- section trick on the Div substrate,
  finite Galois quotient, coproduct assembly -- and states verbatim ''Off-path and
  untouched: Quot-lane sorries''. FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550 marks HasSmoothProperQuotient
  ''PERMANENTLY OFF-PATH ... Do not build new consumers against it'', and Scheme.QuotScheme
  has ZERO consumers. Meanwhile Picard_QuotScheme.tex is 8,434 lines and roadmap nodes
  AJC.picrep.quot / .serre / .assembly still describe it as the strategy. The sunk
  cost is small -- only QuotRepresentability.lean (83 lines) and SerreFiniteness.lean
  (292) are exclusive to the Quot endgame; the other ~9k lines are imported by the
  committed route and must NOT be deleted. Decide: re-aim the blueprint and roadmap
  at the Milne-Kollar route actually being built, or deliberately revive Quot.


  CONTEXT FOR THE DECISION. Representability is months away, not weeks: 18 of the
  campaign''s 28 milestones have zero Lean written (verified by file absence), including
  all of cluster J, the actual Milne construction of Pic^r. Estimate 27k-45k new lines,
  i.e. 22-37% again of the current 121k-line tree; 1-3 months at staffed throughput.
  The single gate is HasRigidPushforward (B3) -- seven direct dependents, and the
  only route in the tree from a line bundle to a DivFamily; it is reduced to ''GeometricallyIntegral
  (p1Over k).hom'', a bounded ~200-350 LOC brick, plus the hfib bridge. The longest
  pole is cluster P (Riemann-Roch chi-ledger, section drops, uniform H^1 vanishing),
  which has ZERO lines in AJC -- but the sibling AJCR has a sorry-free 17,792-line,
  62-module RiemannRoch/ directory that is essentially cluster P. A day auditing AJCR
  for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof
  would.


  ALSO WORTH KNOWING: the headline is unwired. Jacobian.lean imports only AlgebraicJacobian.Genus,
  so none of the 122k lines of Picard/Albanese/Cohomology work is reachable from picardJacobianWitness.
  And two sorry-bodied INSTANCES leak through typeclass synthesis -- instHasPicScheme
  (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:317, sole producer, 41 use sites) and pullback_preservesFiniteLimits
  (CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:163) -- so ''153 sorry-free modules'' is
  a LOCAL claim, not an axiom-cleanliness claim. Run ''#print axioms'' on the headline
  declarations before believing any completeness number.'
